tip: 'Tappa bort' means to lose or misplace, and 'alltid' splits it: 'tappar alltid bort'.
After 'som' a profession normally takes no article: 'jobbat som lärare', worked as a teacher.
'Lite grann' is a fixed phrase meaning a tiny bit; 'grann' here is not 'granne' (neighbor).
For body parts Swedish normally uses the definite form, so 'bröt armen' means broke his arm, not 'bröt sin arm'.
Days of the week are not capitalized in Swedish: 'måndag', not 'Måndag'.
Start with a time word like 'imorgon' and the verb 'är' comes before the subject 'det'.
'Hem' means toward home for motion; being located at home is 'hemma'.
'Vuxit' is the irregular form of 'växa' (to grow) used after 'har'.
After 'är' the adjective adds '-a' for a plural subject: 'vi är glada'.
'Sett' is the irregular form of 'se' (to see) used after 'har'.
'Vunnit' is the form of 'vinna' (to win) used after 'har'; the 'i' shifts to 'u' here.
Clock times use 'klockan': 'landar klockan tre' means lands at three.
'Inga' is the plural of 'ingen': 'inga direktflyg' means no direct flights.
A definite adjective needs both a front word and a noun ending: 'det lilla barnet'.
'Hela' is followed by a definite noun with no extra article: 'hela dagen', the whole day.
'Skrivit' is the form of 'skriva' (to write) used after 'har'.
'Mitt' is the my form for ett-words: 'mitt lösenord'; en-words take 'min' instead.
'Sin' means one's own and refers back to the subject: 'sin plånbok' is her own wallet.
'Att' before a verb marks the infinitive, like English to: 'att flytta' means to move.
'Tänka' pairs with 'på' for about: 'tänkt på saken' means thought about the matter.
'Hört talas om' is a set phrase meaning to have heard about something.
When 'vem' is the subject of a reported question it takes 'som': 'vem som hade ringt'.
'Det finns' (there is/are) works for both singular and plural in Swedish.
After 'med' a means of transport normally drops its article: 'med bil' means by car.
'För att' before a full clause means because: 'för att det snöade'. Before a verb it means in order to.
Past unreal conditions use 'hade' plus the verb's have-form in both halves: 'hade vetat', 'hade kommit'.
'Innan' means before and opens a time clause: 'innan du går', before you leave.
'Nu när' means now that, setting up a current reason: 'nu när du är här'.
'Om' here means if or whether: 'vet inte om han kommer'. In other uses 'om' can mean about.
'Bestämma sig för' means decide on, needing the reflexive 'oss' and 'för': 'bestämt oss för'.
